subject: DPA: data transfer bridgehead & subprocessor onboarding evidence
messages:
From: Clara Jensen <clara.jensen@bridgehealth.io>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@bridgehealth.io
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 08:12:00 +0000
Subject: DPA Qs — scope of transfer & 'bridgehead' concept

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the early engagement. As part of BridgeHealth's DPA review we have a short set of clarifying questions around transfers, subprocessors, and what you refer to internally as the 'bridgehead' or ingestion boundary. We attached our SSQ (short form) — main asks: 

- Can you confirm which subprocessors persist PII-derived artifacts (token logs, KV cache snapshots, telemetry exports)?
- Which geographic locations (region/country) may those subprocessors export data to?
- Define the exact network/processing boundary you call the "bridgehead" (is it a regional gateway, edge proxy, or an aggregate buffer?)
- KMS custody: do you hold keys, or do customers bring their own (BYOK)? Any KMS attestation we can include in the DPA annex?

We'd like to gather evidence (annotated dataflow, subprocessor inventory, KMS snippet) ahead of a 30-minute sync. Can you reply with a short mapping and any artifacts you can share?

Appreciate it,
Clara Jensen
Security & Privacy | BridgeHealth
clara.jensen@bridgehealth.io

Attachment: bridgehealth-ssq-v1.pdf (SSQ PDF)

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Clara Jensen <clara.jensen@bridgehealth.io>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 10:07:00 +0000
Subject: Re: DPA Qs — scope of transfer & 'bridgehead' concept

Hi Clara — thanks for the SSQ. Looping in Marissa (contracts) and Jonas (privacy engineering) to surface the precise artifacts. Quick answers up front:

- Subprocessors that may persist artifacts: inference_shard_ops (token logs for debugging in redact mode), telemetry_collector (aggregated metrics), and vendor-s3 (object storage for archives). We will attach a CSV inventory.
- Cross-border export: default hosted deployment keeps data in the customer-selected region. However, backup/archival exports may be routed to our central archive region for customers who opt-in; we can gate that by contract.
- Bridgehead definition: for Redwood hosted we define the bridgehead as the regional ingress+proxy tier — the short-lived request buffer and early preprocessing (redaction hooks, prefix cache check). It is not long-term storage; KV caches are ephemeral per-model session and live on GPUs.
- KMS: By default Redwood manages KMS keys for hosted customers; we support BYOK via customer-managed KMS (we can provide key-wrap attestation).

Artifacts attached: redwood-annotated-dataflow-v1.pdf, subprocessor-inventory-20261007.csv. We'll follow up with a KMS attestation snippet and a short summary table for retention and egress controls. Can we schedule a 30-min sync Wednesday 14:00 CET?

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Trust & Safety | Redwood Inference
(rishi.malhotra@redwood.com)

Attachments: redwood-annotated-dataflow-v1.pdf, subprocessor-inventory-20261007.csv

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@bridgehealth.io>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: Clara Jensen <clara.jensen@bridgehealth.io>, procurement@bridgehealth.io
Date: Tue, 6 Oct 2026 12:42:00 +0000
Subject: Re: DPA Qs — scope of transfer & 'bridgehead' concept

Thanks Rishi — useful start. A couple of clarifying follow-ups before the call:

1) When you say token logs for debugging are persisted, can you confirm retention windows and whether logs are keyed to customer identifiers or pseudonymized? We need the retention in days and whether logs are stored in plain text.
2) For the 'central archive region' — what regions are in scope and can you provide an export opt-in flag that we can reference in the DPA (we typically require exports to be opt-in and documented in the annex).
3) KMS attestation: we would prefer a short statement we can include in the DPA appendix describing whether Redwood or the customer has access to key material and whether Redwood conducts annual KMS key rotation.

Also attaching a draft DPA clause for transfers (legal_dpa_draft.docx) — can you confirm redlines are acceptable in the sync?

-Liam
Liam O'Connor
Head of Procurement | BridgeHealth
Attachment: legal_dpa_draft.docx

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Clara Jensen <clara.jensen@bridgehealth.io>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@bridgehealth.io>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 09:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: DPA Qs — scope of transfer & 'bridgehead' concept

Hi Clara / Liam — thanks for the clear asks. Adding the specifics you requested below and attaching a geo-mapping spreadsheet. Quick table summary: 

- Token logs (debugging): retained up to 30 days by default, retention configurable down to 0 days on request. Logs are pseudonymized by default (session id + request hash); customer identifiers are not persisted in clear text unless explicitly enabled for debugging.
- Storage format: token logs are stored as UTF-8 text in encrypted objects (AES-256) at rest. Access is limited to a small subset of SREs with audited ACLs.
- Central archive regions: EU-central, US-east, and APAC-sg. Export to a central archive is strictly opt-in and documented in the DPA annex; we will include an "export_opt_in" boolean in the annex template.
- KMS custody: Redwood offers two modes: Redwood-managed KMS (Redwood holds key metadata; key material is wrapped) or Customer-managed (BYOK). We conduct annual key-rotation operations for Redwood-managed keys and can provide a short attestation text.

I attached subproc-geo-mapping.xlsx that maps each subprocessor to region scope and data access purpose. We can accept proposed redlines in the call and mark changes in DocuSign later. Proposed sync: Wed 7 Oct 14:00 CET (30 mins) — Rishi, Jonas and myself will join.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Contracts Manager | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachments: subproc-geo-mapping.xlsx

From: Clara Jensen <clara.jensen@bridgehealth.io>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@bridgehealth.io>, procurement@bridgehealth.io
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 14:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: DPA Qs — scope of transfer & 'bridgehead' concept

Marissa, Rishi — that's perfect and addresses most of our asks. A few quick notes ahead of the sync:

- The retention windows and pseudonymization approach are acceptable; please bring the exact field-level pseudonymization mapping (which headers/ids are redacted) to the call.
- We'll circulate the redlines today; please be prepared for 2 narrow changes (export_opt_in syntax and KMS attestation wording).
- Call confirmed for Wed 7 Oct 14:00 CET — we'll send a calendar invite and include a short agenda: 1) evidence review (5m) 2) DPA annex redlines (15m) 3) KMS attestation wording (10m).

Thanks — looking forward.
Clara
